Special Service and Features
Launch of 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR) Down Folding Butt Version
प्रविष्टि तिथि: 26 AUG 2021 12:51PM by PIB Chennai

In commemoration of 75 years of independence, Ordnance Factory, Tiruchirappalli launched Down folding butt version of 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle on 25th August 2021.  At present, Ordnance Factory, Tiruchirappali, is manufacturing TAR Rifles in two variants i.e. Fixed butt and side folding butt versions.

    The 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle (TAR) is a powerful individual automatic weapon designed to destroy the enemy by fire in single and burst firing mode.  It is a single shot Rifle in normal mode and it can be used in burst mode also.  By firing in burst mode in short series, group or single targets at a range up to 500m can be destroyed.  However, the destructive effect of the TAR is up to a range of 1350m.

          Ordnance Factory, Trichirappallin developed and manufactured TAR  Down folding butt version to meet the customer requirement as some of the CAPF units, State Police and RPF required the Down folding butt version for quick and easy movement of personnel in guard and patrolling duty.

  The overall length of TAR-Down folding butt is 900mm in butt open condition and 650mm in butt folding condition.

 The Down folding butt version of 7.62*39mm Trichy Assault Rifle launched by Shri Sanjay Dwivedi, IOFS, General Manager, Ordnance Factory, Trichirappalli and Shri Rajiv Jain, IOFS, Addl. General Manager, Shri A.K.Singh, IOFS, Addl.General Manager Shri V. Gunasekaran, IOFS, Joint General Manager, Shri S. Krishanaswamy, IOFS, Joint General Manager and other Officers of OFT attended the function.

Lets make one thing clear : Ghatak Rifle is nothing but an Indianized Mpi KM-72 with the similar stamped receiver as INSAS 1b1. Trichy Assault Rifle is an Indianized AR-M1 featuring a milled receiver.

![Image 3](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-ad71828cff7640f93d4cff74a49d2a00-lq)

Trichy Rifle with telescopic buttstock————————————

There are two versions of Trichy : one based on FN FAL while another based on basic Kalashnikov Design while using the same AK-47 7.62x39mm rounds. The FN FAL version was rejected by the Army leading Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli (OFT) to work on a Kalashnikov variant. There is a fire selector on right, with the magazine release of AK's paddle type lock.

![Image 4](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-14011322a2e23b7f3bcf9545338dcff4-pjlq)

Trichy Assault Rifle———————————

It does not feature Ambidextrous Controls which is featured on many other contemporary rifles. Trichy features AK-47 style front sight post with larger width as opposed to AKM style Front Sight Post with smaller width. While, Ghatak features aperture fixed on traditional AK style sights.

![Image 5](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-8a849b9bda5d8ce480b8daab0bdc1ef2-lq)

P-Rails are there on Ghaatak's handgrip but not on Trichy,although FAB type upgrades can be installed on both. Trichy features various buttstock configurations like Side Folder ones (Galil Style),Underfolder ones (AK underfolder ones) and fixed AKM style ones including a telescopic buttstock.

![Image 6](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-a0420b2b082e9611813b3984c6f3cb46-lq)

ITBP Troopers with Ghatak Rifle—————————

Overall Trichy is a much better , improved and refined version of Kalashnikov than Ghatak thanks to its better milled receiver , wide configuration of stocks available and more ergonomic to modern-day soldier.

![Image 26](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-635bb7740387cd12d59aae3719a577b5.webp)

Army has taken a crucial decision regarding equipping it’s soldiers with modern assault rifle. This is what the COAS. Gen Bipin rawat has to say regarding the issue:

\> Since a state-of-the-art assault rifle will cost about Rs 200,000 each in the global market, let us issue these only to front line infantry soldiers who confront the enemy armed only with their rifles.Let us provide a cheaper indigenous option to other soldiers, for whom the rifle is not a primary weapon.

Total of 800000 rifles are to be procured and there distribution is as explained below.

![Image 27](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-9a9e999b3940f2f4981f9b3394112f90)

SMALL DESCRIPTION:

HAND GUARD:

![Image 28](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-ac425656b8f00d83fd4bb321fde5f0a1.webp)

Its hand guard due to its ergonomic design, the tactical hand-guard has build in quad rail ( Mil specs ) but has much surface covers with smooth fiber, Unlike the once made of complete aluminum are uncomfortable when used in long run without using gloves, In our Army and paramilitary gloves are not an part of fighting kit, Keeping this in mind the design solves the problem.

![Image 29](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-89143a8a266591ff21d50eae13bc8198.webp)

The side rails are most resourceful which are again missing from present serving AK and AKMs, for mounting flash light and essential gadgets in today's war.

PISTOL GRIP:

![Image 30](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-99d7183c6c6913172931611a7f8f5f51.webp)

This grip is originally from Amogh Carbine, Unlike 1B1\`s or more accurately AK47\`s grip from 60s, This grip is designed keeping ergonomic in mind. The grip is angled and has slots or curves for pre positioning of fingers to place in, Its texture has tiny embedded dots all over its body for a tight and non slippery griping.

SIGHTS:

![Image 31](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-a6b2c3f4f9a0234b6c497d1bf6d50a17.webp)

![Image 32](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-ccfa7c13f97c353bb22b7ee50371fdc1.webp)

Iron sights are most interesting feature on this Assault rifle and perhaps impressed me the most, The front sights are H&K style front sights, Where as the rear sight is hybrid AK and INSAS 1B1 leaf sight though not foldable.Such a feature will boost confidence while engaging targets at medium range with far better accuracy then using open sights trying to find the tip between the rear sights.

RECIEVER, GAS BLOCK and MUZZLE BREAK:

![Image 33](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-8844c241874ff6ffa88da1dd0330912a.webp)

The basic outer look of the receiver is same as other AK\`s around the world, It has the similar selector switch which has similar modes, One is semi other is fully auto and safety, The cocking / charging handle are all similar to an AK\`s, However the magazine release and trigger so does assembly is from INSAS 1B1 when looked closely.

The receiver is most mysterious part of this rifle, As its looks similar to any other AK\`s in the world while its internal working makes its most different than other AK\`s around the world.

![Image 34](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-8f0bb3974a4430c7328e45ae0fe8571d.webp)

Here the 45 degree gas block is originally from AK design, The barrel is chromed line and its a 16inch one, The front sight is H&K style and the muzzle brake is slant one like found on original design, The muzzle brake is a simple yet efficient design which effectively reduce muzzle climb and rightward muzzle drift during rapid fire.

The Magazine here is a license copy of Bulgarian Waffle style 30rnd AK magazine, This get really heavy when fully loaded nearly around 700gms, And their are metal tabs in this which stop it from shredding, Its perhaps the best choice for Ghatak as its this magazine is consider best design.

The design is best trade off between strength, Reliability and durability, The magazine has steel reinforcement at various places which increase its durability over other fiber magazine available for AK, Its solid design for Indian requirement which can take harsh punishment from a solider and from nature.

Trichy Assault Rifles can well be touted the Indianized Bulgarian AR-M1 featuring a milled receiver as opposed to the stamped receiver similar to INSAS 1b1 present on Ghatak Rifle. It has quite minor differences to AR-M1 with minor difference in gas block,which is of completely flat front profile.

![Image 39](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-ad71828cff7640f93d4cff74a49d2a00-lq)

There are two versions of Trichy : one based on FN FAL while another based on basic Kalashnikov Design while using the same AK-47 7.62x39mm rounds. The FN FAL version was rejected by the Army leading Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli (OFT) to work on a Kalashnikov variant. There is a fire selector on right, with the magazine release of AK's paddle type lock.

![Image 40](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-14011322a2e23b7f3bcf9545338dcff4-pjlq)

It does not feature Ambidextrous Controls which is featured on many other contemporary rifles. Trichy features AK-47 style front sight post with larger width as opposed to AKM style Front Sight Post with smaller width.

P-Rails are there on Ghaatak's handgrip but not on Trichy,although FAB type upgrades can be installed on both. Trichy features various buttstock configurations like Side Folder ones (Galil Style),Underfolder ones (AK underfolder ones) and fixed AKM style ones including a telescopic buttstock.

![Image 41](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-8a849b9bda5d8ce480b8daab0bdc1ef2-lq)

Trichy has a Rate of Fire of 600-650 rounds per minute with a practical rate of fire being 120-125 rounds per minute.

Overall this is a GOOD rifle suited for Indian conditions and forces who tend to favour AKs . It is best suited to replace the expensive imported AKs which India bought in surplus from Romania , Bulgaria and East Germany.

 · [8y](https://www.quora.com/What-is-the-difference-between-an-assault-rifle-and-a-battle-rifle/answer/Dag-Erik-Bottolfsen)

Short answer:

Battle rifles fire full-sized rifle cartriges, while assault rifles fire scaled down intermediate calibres.

When the Germans invented the assault rifle (Sturmgevehr) they took a rifle bullet and basically halved the size of the cartridge, because they realized that putting the full 7,92mm rifle cartridge in a shoulder-fired full auto weapon would make it damn near uncontrollable. An added benefit of the scaled down cartridge was that it made the soldier capable of carrying more rounds.

That is actually quite an intensive question taking into the fact that there a variety of Indian Special Forces and Commando units and each operator and unit has their own specific preference in regards to the personal weapon they are equipped with. The choice also depends on the sort of operation they are going to conduct or undertake. Swift Operations involving hit-and-run operations may see intermediate caliber weapons at use like a Tavor or a Kalashnikov. While in other cases like Close Quarter Battle Situations , an Assault Rifle is rarely used. Special Forces Operators either prefer a Carbine or Submachine Gun in this case as they are more compact in Close Quarters.

![Image 47](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-90f8503a520e4e1cf5075477d8272303-lq)

Earlier , Indian Army Paratrooper Special Forces preferred the good old Vz.58 Assault Rifles. Vz.58 sports many features which gives it a traditional preference by Special Forces Operators over the ubiquitous Kalashnikov Platform. Vz.58 is no AK since it has not interchangeable parts with the Kalashnikov Platform including the magazine. The only similarity between them is the Soviet 7.62x39mm Round for which both the Rifles are chambered. Vz.58 features a Short Stroke Gas Piston System including a striker fired mechanism. Vz.58 features more quality build-up than AKs due to its Milled Receiver and also had a Bolt Hold-Open Feature which helps the operator to be alerted when the magazine is out.

![Image 48](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-f3b4ac40fa35af46014666256da42aab-lq)

Vz.58 was retired in the early half of 2000s and was replaced with Tavors in active service. Tavor featured much more advancements than AK or Vz.58 platform since it was an ultra-modern 21st Century-era firearm and coul mount various Sights and Accessories on user's demand. Tavor slowly became one of the favorite of Indian Special Forces units and the staple firearm in all three Indian Special Forces units : Para SF , MARCOS and Garud Commando Force. Tavor featured many variants pertaining to user demands like GTAR-21 ( Grenadier Variant ) , STAR-21 ( For Sharpshooters ) and CTAR-21 ( Compact Variant for CQBs ). All the variants featured interchangeable parts and magazines which overall increased the efficiency of Special Forces team to share ammunition during long operations. Other than this , the Bullpup Configuration of Tavor which helped the rifle to overall reduce its length retaining its barrel length made it a primary choice especially in CQB situations.

![Image 49](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-ff0b72629c227b355ee1d50247f92ba2-lq)

Another Rifle which is more preferred by Indian Special Forces units are the Kalashnikovs. The prime reason for this choice is the extreme reliability and ruggedness including the 7.62x39mm round which is effective in Close to Medium Range Gunfights.

![Image 50](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-be216b895f80025677f8c5dcf6b0279e-lq)

The older Kalashnikovs are being upgraded by TDI Arms , FAB Defense MOD and OFB to modern standards by adding P-Rails and various other accessories like a Foregrip , Foldable Buttstock , Reflex Sights and Polymer Handguards. It increases the overall efficiency of the Kalashnikov Platform giving the operator a freedom to customize his personal weapon as per his freedom. MARCOS also uses the modern AK-103 which is actually an AK-74M chambered for 7.62x39mm rounds.

![Image 51](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-82950de8d8c18c94fa1d9d3493cb512a-lq)

Another Assault Rifle which is widely used by various Indian State Commando Units is the SIG SG550 Rifle Series. Variants of SG550 Rifle series are utilized by various Indian Commando units and even National Security Guard ( NSG ). NSG utilizes the SG553 LB ( Longer Barrel Variant ) besides SG551SB and SG553SB which are Shorter Barrel variant. Haryana Police 'Tiger' Commando Unit , Madhya Pradesh 'Hawk' Commando unit and Jharkhand Jaguars utilizes the SG551LB Variant. The SG550 Rifle variants are slowly becoming one of the most preferred Assault Rifle among various Indian units primarily due to its conventional layout , ultra-modern features , Long Stroke Gas Piston and high Reliability.

![Image 52](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-0198092d3b5a85785d6275a6c92a4fe4-lq)

SIG SG551LB with Trijicon ACOG Sight in service with Haryana Police Commandos

So the question still larges loom on which Assault Rifle do Indian Special Forces like the most. At the end this question is more intensive on the type of job and the operator preference regarding weapons. AKs and Vz.58 are more preferred during Counter-Terrorism Operations since their heavy 7.62mm ammo provides the desired hydrostatic shock which is fundamental in stopping tangos during heavy firefight. Assault Rifles like Tavors and SG550 variants are mainly utilized for swift raids and strikes as they are chambered for a lighter intermediate round and can sport various accessories and features as per user preference. It also allows the operator to carry more ammo in the battlefield and is also quite effective at long ranges.

![Image 53](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-173e6c91dc9763ee1b3e05079b0cbad1-lq)

Tier 1 Units have now started using more modern Battle Rifles which utilize a more powerful 7.62x51mm Full-Powered Rifle Cartridge as they overcome the traditional deficiencies of the Intermediate Rounds and feature more stopping power and ballistic performance. Tier 1 Units have started using Battle Rifles like SCAR-H and CM-901 for Assault Purposes and SIG-716 as a Designated Marksman Rifle. These Battle Rifles overcome the deficiencies of older designs giving a more ergonomic design to Special Forces Operators with freedom to attach various accessories and tactical modifications. These rifles are now being increasingly inducted into Indian Special Operations Units alongside other rifles like Tavors.

As it turns out…..no. During use in Afghanistan a fairly serious problem with the rifle turned up, namely the rifle had virtually no chance of hitting it’s target in combat. It was discovered that even when clamped in a bench rest only 7 out of 100 bullets fired hit a target at 100 meters, an appallingly bad level of accuracy. And the target? Not some pie plate size bulls eye…..a 6 x 3 sheet of plywood. The apparent reason is that composite parts of the rifle warp in temperatures over 80 degrees F. What makes the story even more appalling is that apparently Heckler & Koch, the rifle’s manufacturer, and the German government, who was paying for them, had known of the problem for a long time and had chosen to ignore it and send German troops to Afghanistan, a place where foreigners get shot at frequently, armed with this piece of crap. The rifle’s accuracy was so bad that when attacked German troops did not even bother to fire back with their rifles, instead choosing to focus completely on bringing their crew served machine guns into action.

A little research into the G-36 turns up an alarming fact. The rifle was developed from a concept drawing. This by the way is not an uncommon way to design things but in the case of firearms it means that the “designers” are trying to shoe horn parts into an already predetermined package and is an excellent recipe for disaster which is exactly what the G-36 is. The “designers” (and the customers)were more concerned about how the weapon looked than how it functioned. It’s basically a piston driven AR-15 with a bunch of cheap plastic parts shoe horned into futuristic body that the Germans were gambling they’d never have to use in combat. Because it’s a piston driven AR it’s at least reliable and people may be afraid that you’re shooting at them but that’s about it.

About the only humorous part of the story is that there are stupid people in America who tried to foist either this rifle or it’s progeny, the XM-8, on the US military because it was “German engineering” which was somehow magically better.

I am certain that my lack of reverence for “German engineering” will raise some hackles among some Quora users but before you start I’ve owned a few German cars and the more experience I’ve gained with them the less respect I have…….
